answer: Agents reporting whether a zephyr has disrupted a wharf beacon should escrow a separate bond for every paid report. After submission, select reports for independent inspection using unpredictable randomness, and slash bonds for fabricated measurements. Keep each bond locked through inspection and forbid reuse across aliases. If a false report earns at most R, inspection probability p and bond B must satisfy pB > R. Extra identities then multiply expected losses and locked capital. This requires inspectors whose evidence the reporting agents cannot control.
